subject: Clarifications: Evaluation scope, EU AI Act classification, and evidence schedule
raw_thread:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@harbormed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: HarborMed Procurement <procurement@harbormed.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: EU AI Act classification & evidence we should expect

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A couple of clarifications from our side before we proceed to scoring:

1) Classification: We need a short rationale for whether Redwood considers the referenced models in scope as "high-risk" under the EU AI Act (Article 6–7) for healthcare triage use cases. If you assess there is a subset that may be high-risk, please identify the criteria used.

2) Evidence deliverables: What artifacts do you intend to provide as part of the RFP response and subsequent PO? Examples: model lineage, eval harness repo, regression results, SOC2-like operational evidence, sample audit logs.

3) Timeline: We prefer a 6-week window from contract signature to delivery of the initial evidence pack (evaluation results + audit log samples). Can you confirm feasibility and highlight any prerequisites?

Appreciate concise responses — scoring will include clarity and reproducibility.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, HarborMed

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: EU AI Act classification & evidence we should expect

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, detail and attachments below.

1) Classification: We evaluate risk at the product+deployment level. For a clinical triage workflow with automated recommendations but clinician-in-the-loop review, our baseline assessment is "special category / potential high-risk depending on decision-making autonomy and regulatory role." In short: likely not automatically high-risk in a supervised clinician-in-loop configuration, but could be high-risk if the model output directly determines care pathways. We'll provide a decision checklist that highlights the boundary conditions.

2) Evidence deliverables (we will provide):
  - RMF mapping summary (NIST AI RMF to our controls) — attachment: RMF_Mapping_Summary.docx
  - Evaluation schedule and milestones (Eval_Schedule.xlsx)
  - RFP assessment matrix with traceability to artifacts (RFP_Redwood_Assessment_Matrix.pdf)
  - Regression harness readme and sample results (Regression_Harness_Readme.md)
  - Sample audit logs and retention policy extract (included as part of evidence pack)

3) Timeline: 6 weeks is achievable with two prerequisites: signed MSA with evidence-sharing clauses, and confirmation of the scope (which models + datasets you expect in evaluation). With those we propose:
  - Week 1: Kickoff, scope finalize, access approvals for any customer test data (if applicable)
  - Weeks 2–4: Evaluation runs, NIST mapping and EU classification write-up
  - Week 5: Regression sampling and reproducibility package assembly
  - Week 6: Delivery of evidence pack + optional walkthrough session

I've attached the assessment matrix and a proposed schedule. Neha — can you review the EU classification write-up and add any compliance caveats?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RFP_Redwood_Assessment_Matrix.pdf (pdf), Eval_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Question: EU AI Act classification & evidence we should expect

Aisha — confirming feasibility and attaching the one-pager and supporting artifacts. Summary below; full artifacts in attachments and the shared Drive link.

Executive summary (one paragraph)
Redwood assesses risk by feature and deployment: for clinician-in-loop triage our current assessment is that the deployment is not inherently high-risk provided the customer mandates explicit human oversight, documents intended purpose, and keeps an audit trail. Where the model output is used to autonomously trigger clinical decisions we classify the deployment as high-risk and recommend a higher-discipline evidence package (expanded sampling, third-party verification).

Deliverables (what you will receive within 6 weeks after signed agreement):
- RMF mapping summary (NIST AI RMF functions + our control mapping) — RMF_Mapping_Summary.docx
- EU classification checklist + decision flow (one-pager) — included in the assessment matrix PDF
- Evaluation harness repository (tagged release) + readme — Regression_Harness_Readme.md + GitHub link
- Regression sampling report (sampling methodology, test-set selection, pre/post deploy comparisons) — sample CSVs included
- Sample audit logs (anonymized subset, with schema) and retention policy extract
- Walkthrough session and Q&A (60–90 minutes)

Evaluation & regression approach (high level)
- Scope: We will run the suite against the three model variants you listed in the RFP (v1.2, v1.3-quant, v2-llm). If you add customer test data we will execute an additional reproducibility run under NDA.
- Sampling: stratified random sampling across clinical intent categories; typical sampling target is 2–5% of production traffic or a minimum of 5k examples per model, whichever is greater. For initial RFP evidence we provide 5k representative eval samples unless you prefer a specific distribution.
- Metrics: accuracy-like clinical labeling (task dependent), false negative rate (FNR) by subgroup, calibration curves, hallucination incidence, and a token-level feature importance summary when applicable.
- Regression criteria: we flag a regression if any safety-critical metric degrades beyond a signed threshold (e.g., +2% absolute FNR). We provide suggested thresholds; final thresholds are customer-negotiable.
- CI & reproducibility: evaluation harness runs as a CI job (GitHub Actions) with immutable artifacts: container image digest, test-set hash, and logged output. We provide a recorded run and the harness repository with a tagged release.

Data & privacy notes:
- Audit logs provided will be anonymized and schema-limited; full production logs require a separate agreement.
- We can perform an on-prem replay of customer data in a dedicated environment if HarborMed requires no data egress. This is scoped as an add-on.

Open items / asks for HarborMed to confirm:
- Confirm final model list and any additional test datasets you want included.
- Confirm whether you want the on-prem replay option (add-on pricing).
- Approved point of contact for contract language on evidence sharing (procurement legal).

Next steps: if this matches your expectations we will drop the one-pager in the shared Drive (link below), attach the evaluation harness tag, and propose a kickoff date upon PO signature.
